checkIn.arrivalMessage: The full address is 49 Timberline Rd N, Sunrise Mountain Village, Unit A3, Killington, VT. Check-in is any time after 4:00 PM.
checkIn.parkingNote: Park in the lot directly in front of the unit. Please don't block the fire hydrant or any stairways or walkways. We'd appreciate no more than 2 cars if possible, parked as close to the unit as you can. The lot is plowed regularly in winter and during storms, but exact timing isn't guaranteed, especially during a big one.
checkIn.linensNote: All the beds have been made up with fresh linens and towels, ready for you.

additionalNotes.label: Firewood & fireplace
additionalNotes.text: Firewood is available in the sheds in the parking lot — please close the shed door after you grab some. See the Fireplace & Firewood section below for the full rules.

additionalNotes.label: Ski trail map
additionalNotes.text: A map of the ski-in/ski-out trails is posted in the hallway.

skiInstructions.warning: Ski-on/ski-off access is snow-dependent and not guaranteed during your trip. Typically ski-on/ski-off is available from January through March.
skiInstructions.skiOn: Exit the parking lot and turn right toward the main street. Take a left onto the main street and walk a few seconds until you reach the ski-on trail. Snap into your skis there and ski down to the Sunrise Lift, which connects to Bear Mountain and the rest of the resort.
skiInstructions.skiOff: Ski down Bear Cub trail. You'll come to the Sunrise Trail on your right — don't take it, it leads all the way to the Sunrise Lift, which is a long hike back to the condo. Instead, stay to the right on Bear Cub, and a few seconds past that junction you'll see a gate on the side of the trail (pictured below). Ski around the gate onto the community trail, then follow it for a few minutes — you'll pass several condo buildings — until it reaches the road. Take your skis off there; the condo is just across the street.
skiInstructions.snowboarding: There are some flat sections on the ski-on/ski-off route, so it takes more effort to snowboard in and out than to ski. It's doable, just not always the most fun.

fireplace.intro: The fireplace is yours to enjoy during your stay — just a few rules to keep everyone safe and the place in good shape for the next guests:
rules: Leave the flue open at all times — please never close it.
Keep the fire contained inside the fireplace at all times, and make sure the fireplace gate is closed in front of it any time a fire is burning.
Don't leave the property while there's an active fire.
Make sure the fire is completely out before heading to bed for the night.
Firewood is provided at no cost in the wood shed in the parking lot — please close the shed doors after grabbing some.
Carry firewood carefully so it doesn't scratch or dirty the floors, and keep it in the dedicated wood storage by the fireplace rather than stacking it elsewhere in the condo.
Keep the fire under control at all times, and use good judgment.
Before you check out, please clean up any ashes and restock the wood storage by the fireplace for the next guests.

items.name: Snow tubing at Killington Resort
items.note: Groomed tubing lanes with a lift back up — easy fun for any age.

items.name: Ski or ride Pico Mountain
items.note: Killington's quieter sister resort just down the road — fewer crowds, same Green Mountain terrain.

items.name: Snowshoe or cross-country ski at Gifford Woods State Park
items.note: Quiet, scenic trails through mature hardwood forest.

items.name: Ride the K-1 Express Gondola to the summit
items.note: A scenic ride to 4,241 feet, even if you're not skiing that day.

items.name: Killington Distillery tasting
items.note: Local spirits, a short drive from the condo.

items.name: Hike Thundering Brook Falls Trail
items.note: A short boardwalk trail to a waterfall running strong with snowmelt.

items.name: Kayak Kent Pond
items.note: Guided kayak tours as the ice clears, through Appalachian Trail Adventures.

items.name: Watch the maple syrup boil at Maple Sugar & Vermont Spice
items.note: A working sugarhouse restaurant — watch syrup made on-site from the gallery dining room.

items.name: Vermont Maple Open House Weekend
items.note: A late-March statewide weekend when local sugarhouses open for tours and tastings.

items.name: Explore Gifford Woods State Park as it reopens
items.note: Early-season hiking and the first camping of the year.

items.name: Killington Bike Park
items.note: The East's largest lift-served mountain biking destination — 30+ miles of trail for every level.

items.name: Killington Adventure Center
items.note: Mountain coaster, zip lines, climbing wall, and a gondola ride up the mountain.

items.name: Kayak or paddleboard Kent Pond
items.note: Rentals and guided tours (they also do cave exploring) through Appalachian Trail Adventures.

items.name: Golf at Killington Resort
items.note: An 18-hole mountain course with sweeping Green Mountain views.

items.name: Ride the K-1 Express Gondola to the summit
items.note: Cool off at 4,241 feet and grab lunch at the Peak Lodge.

items.name: Fall foliage gondola ride
items.note: The K-1 Express Gondola runs scenic foliage rides through October.

items.name: Hike Thundering Brook Falls Trail
items.note: A short, easy trail — especially pretty with the fall color in.

items.name: Mountain bike the Killington Bike Park
items.note: The bike park stays open into fall — riding through peak foliage is a local favorite.

items.name: Gifford Woods State Park
items.note: Fall camping and hiking through mature hardwoods at their most colorful.

items.name: Rooftop deck at The Lookout Tavern
items.note: Widely considered the best foliage view in town, with dinner and a drink.

favoriteRestaurants.name: The Lookout Tavern
favoriteRestaurants.note: Killington's go-to casual spot — famous wings, craft beer, and a rooftop deck with mountain views.

favoriteRestaurants.name: Sunup Bakery
favoriteRestaurants.note: Counter-service bakery for breakfast sandwiches, pastries, and coffee — grab-and-go before hitting the mountain.

favoriteRestaurants.name: Charity's 1887 Saloon
favoriteRestaurants.note: A Killington classic since 1971, built around an antique bar shipped over from a 1887 West Virginia saloon. Famous French onion soup.

favoriteRestaurants.name: Liquid Art Restaurant
favoriteRestaurants.note: Family-run coffeehouse-meets-restaurant with local art on the walls — breakfast, dinner, and craft cocktails.

favoriteRestaurants.name: Casey's Caboose
favoriteRestaurants.note: A one-of-a-kind dinner in a retired 1900 railroad snowplow car — a Killington tradition since 1981.

favoriteRestaurants.name: The Garlic
favoriteRestaurants.note: Cozy, Tuscan-inspired Italian — walk-in only, so arrive right at opening to skip the line.

favoriteRestaurants.name: The Foundry at Summit Pond
favoriteRestaurants.note: Killington's fine-dining destination on the water — locally sourced, chef-driven menu with a 100+ bottle wine list.

communityCenter.intro: As part of your stay, you have access to Sunrise Mountain Village's community center — Sunrise Commons & Sports Center. Hours and amenities shift with the season, so check the website below if you have questions, but here's what's typically available to guests:
amenities: Indoor heated pool, hot tub, sauna, and steam room during the winter season, plus a year-round outdoor hot tub and outdoor pool
A private sports center with cardio and strength training equipment
Free equipment to borrow — ice skates, snowshoes, cross-country skis and poles, sleds, and Puff Hockey gear, all from the Snowshoe Hut behind Sunrise Commons
An outdoor ice skating pond, backcountry trails, and a patio with a gas fire pit
The Hideout — a short, solar-lit walk down the Village Pond Trail to a unique nighttime spot
Seasonal hours at the on-site Sunrise Bar & Grill
communityCenter.websiteLabel: Sunrise Mountain Village — hours, amenities & FAQs

checkOut.trash: Please remove any trash and recycling and place it in the appropriate bins by the woodshed in the driveway. Trash and recycling should be taken out before 1:00 PM.
checkOut.sheetsTowels: For any linens or towels you used, please leave them in a pile on the floor of the room they were used in.
checkOut.windows: Please make sure all windows and doors are closed and locked.
checkOut.thermostat: Please leave the thermostats at 65 degrees — no higher, no lower.
checkOut.shedYard: If you used the fireplace, please remove any ash, place it in the ash bucket, and empty the bucket in the dedicated spot by the woodshed in the driveway. If you used any firewood, we'd appreciate it being replaced and re-stacked in the woodshed for the next guests.
